# Embedded CPU temperature

Nexo uses the official LibreHardwareMonitorLib NuGet package 0.9.6 inside its own process. It enables CPU hardware only and opens, updates, and attempts to close the computer for each measurement, including error/cancellation paths. No standalone Libre Hardware Monitor program or WMI publisher is needed.

In LibreHardwareMonitorLib 0.9.6, `Open()` can fail after acquiring resources but before marking the computer open; `Close()` can then return without releasing that partial initialization. Nexo cannot guarantee cleanup in that upstream failure path. A process-wide circuit breaker prevents any later `Open()` after an initialization failure and reports that restarting Nexo allows another attempt. Read/update failures after successful initialization do not trip this breaker. Storage collection remains independent.

CPU register access requires the separately installed PawnIO driver on supported Windows hardware. Nexo does not install or launch its installer. Missing PawnIO gives `no_source` and a null temperature. A present driver does not guarantee access: permissions, platform support, or security settings may leave `no_sensor`/`error`. No estimated temperature is substituted. This change does not elevate Nexo automatically.

On the development host, a standard non-administrator process detected installed PawnIO 2.1.0.0 with its service running, but opening the PawnIO device with the library's ReadWrite access returned Windows error 5 (access denied). LibreHardwareMonitorLib 0.9.6 exposed only `Core (Tctl/Tdie)`, returning raw zero on two updates one second apart. This is not a real temperature reading; Nexo reports `invalid`, null Celsius, and a possible hardware-access permission limitation. The standard host session therefore has no usable CPU temperature with this integration. Driver installation alone does not resolve that permission boundary, and Nexo does not automatically elevate its full process.

Temperature and storage collection remain independent. Temperature has a 10-second managed wait limit. A native call cannot safely be terminated in-process; if it exceeds the wait limit or the caller cancels, disposal is attempted when that call returns. A process-wide gate prevents another hardware session from starting while the first still runs. The storage PowerShell process keeps its separate 15-second limit.

The official library is distributed unmodified under MPL-2.0. Its source is available at https://github.com/LibreHardwareMonitor/LibreHardwareMonitor/tree/3d331e3370efb858411f19511373eff65a218701 (the commit identified by the NuGet package). License and upstream third-party notices accompany Nexo in `ThirdParty/LibreHardwareMonitor`. PawnIO bytecode license is also included; no PawnIO driver installer is bundled by Nexo. Keep these notices when redistributing binaries and retain the source availability link. Transitive package licensing remains applicable.
